idiom_name: duck typing; typing.Protocol for statically checked structural contracts
implementation_notes: Python never had the storage problem: any object can be held in any variable and behaviour is selected by attribute lookup at call time, so unrelated classes participate in one interface merely by defining the right methods. Protocol (PEP 544, Python 3.8+) adds a statically checkable form of the same contract - a class becomes a structural subtype of the protocol without inheriting from it - while staying a type-checker concept at runtime: @runtime_checkable isinstance only tests that the members exist, never their signatures. The collections.abc ABCs (Iterable, Sized, Callable) remain the nominal, runtime-checkable option and are what the typing protocols are modelled on.
pitfalls: Protocols are a static-checker concept: nothing validates the shape at run time unless @runtime_checkable is used, and that check only confirms the members exist.
Data protocols (attributes) cannot be used with isinstance safely at all, and issubclass works only for non-data protocols - protocol checks on dynamically set attributes misreport.
Duck typing hides contract breaks until execution: a renamed method fails only when that path runs, so the protocol belongs in the tests, not just in the annotations.
